pillars.name: Access
pillars.blurb: Whether an assistant is allowed to read the site at all, and whether the site says so consistently.

signals.label: robots.txt does not block the site
signals.why: A blanket Disallow is the end of the conversation. Nothing below it matters, because nothing gets read.
signals.fix: Narrow the Disallow to the paths that actually needed it.

signals.label: The site serves a robots.txt
signals.why: Most assistants fetch it before anything else. A missing one is not a block, but it is the file where a site gets to say which crawlers it wants.
signals.fix: Serve a robots.txt, even one that allows everything and names the sitemap.

signals.label: robots.txt and llms.txt agree
signals.why: A site that publishes llms.txt is addressing assistants directly. When robots.txt then blocks the ones it welcomes, the two files disagree and the crawler obeys robots.txt.
signals.fix: Decide which assistants may read the site, then say the same thing in both files.

signals.label: The site publishes an llms.txt
signals.why: llms.txt is how a site tells an assistant which pages are the ones worth reading. Without it an assistant works from the sitemap and the navigation, like a crawler.
signals.fix: Write /llms.txt listing the pages you would want quoted. `--write-llms` generates a first draft from this crawl.

signals.label: No AI crawler is disallowed
signals.why: Blocking GPTBot or ClaudeBot is a deliberate choice and costs nothing here. It is reported because it decides the ceiling on everything below: a crawler that is refused never reads the page it would have quoted.
signals.fix: Nothing, unless the block was not intended.

pillars.name: Answer engines
pillars.blurb: Whether there is a passage an assistant can lift whole and attribute, rather than a page it has to summarise itself.

signals.label: Pages answer a question in a liftable passage
signals.why: An assistant quotes a passage, not a page. With no question-shaped heading answered underneath it, it has to summarise the page and attribute the summary to itself.
signals.fix: Give the page a heading that asks what a reader would ask, and answer it in the paragraph underneath.

signals.label: No page forbids its own snippet
signals.why: nosnippet, max-snippet:0 and data-nosnippet withhold the exact text an answer engine would have quoted. The page can still be read; it cannot be repeated.
signals.fix: Drop the directive on pages you want quoted, or narrow it to the element that needed it.

signals.label: Pages are mostly their own content
signals.why: When most of the words are navigation, footer and chrome, an assistant weighing what the page is about is reading mostly furniture.
signals.fix: Put the content in <main> and keep the furniture out of it.

signals.label: Pages name an author
signals.why: Experience and expertise are the first two letters of E-E-A-T, and neither can be read off a page that names nobody.
signals.fix: Name the author in the structured data, not only in the byline image.

pillars.name: Generative engines
pillars.blurb: Whether the page carries what a model weighs when it decides which of two sources to cite.

signals.label: No hidden text addresses the model
signals.why: Text hidden from the reader and served to the crawler, shaped like an instruction, is read as manipulation — and it is the page, not the passage, that stops being trusted.
signals.fix: Remove it. If it arrived with a plugin or a template, it is worth knowing it is being served.

signals.label: Pages cite a source
signals.why: The largest single effect in the Princeton GEO study (+30–115% visibility). An assistant weighing two pages prefers the one that shows its work.
signals.fix: Link out from inside the content to the sources the claims rest on.

signals.label: Pages carry concrete numbers
signals.why: Second-largest effect in the same study (+40%). A number is the part of a page an assistant can quote as a fact rather than paraphrase as an opinion.
signals.fix: Give the figure, the percentage or the year rather than "significantly".

signals.label: Pages quote someone
signals.why: An attributed quote — name, role, year — was worth +30–40% in the same study, and is the cheapest expertise signal a page can carry.
signals.fix: Quote a named person in a <blockquote> with a <cite>.

signals.label: No passage is too long to quote
signals.why: Retrieval splits a page into passages and quotes one. A paragraph running to the length of a page is quoted whole or not at all.
signals.fix: Break the passage at the points where it changes subject.
